shorts.title: The Pig War of 1859 Was REAL 🐷 Case #7 Meatball Investigates
shorts.description:
A farmer shot a pig, and two empires sent warships. In 1859 an American farmer on San Juan Island shot a Hudson's Bay Company pig that was eating his potatoes. The standoff grew to 461 US soldiers against five Royal Navy warships carrying 2,140 men. Nobody fired on the other side, and the only casualty was the pig. In 1872 an arbitration chosen by German Emperor Wilhelm I gave the islands to the US.

#shorts #meatballinvestigates #weirdhistory #mystery #meatballmyths

shorts.title: The US Really Built BAT BOMBS 🦇 Case #9 Meatball Investigates
shorts.description:
Bats carrying tiny bombs flew loose and set an air base on fire. Project X-Ray: in WWII the US strapped small timed incendiaries to Mexican free-tailed bats. On 15 May 1943 escaped bats set fire to the Carlsbad Army Airfield Auxiliary Air Base in New Mexico. The idea came from a dentist, Lytle Adams, and President Roosevelt approved it.

#shorts #meatballinvestigates #weirdhistory #mystery #meatballmyths

shorts.title: The CIA Really Built a Spy Cat 🐈 Case #10 Meatball Investigates
shorts.description:
Spies wired a microphone inside a cat's ear. Project Acoustic Kitty: in the 1960s a CIA veterinary surgeon put a microphone in a cat's ear canal and a transmitter at the base of its skull. A 1967 memo concluded trained cats weren't practical for real spying, and the project was cancelled.

shorts.title: The Gulf of Tonkin Attack That Never Happened 🔍 Case #11 Meatball Investigates
shorts.description:
A US destroyer fired into the dark at enemy boats. On 2 August 1964 USS Maddox really fought North Vietnamese torpedo boats. The second 'attack', on 4 August, was based on bad intelligence: a declassified NSA history (2005) concluded it never happened. Congress passed the Gulf of Tonkin Resolution on 7 August 1964.

#shorts #meatballinvestigates #weirdhistory #mystery #meatballmyths

shorts.title: The Ghost Ship Mary Celeste: What REALLY Happened? 👻 Case #12
shorts.description:
Sailors found a ship adrift, and nobody aboard. The Mary Celeste was found adrift near the Azores on 4 December 1872, seaworthy, with plenty of food and water and her lifeboat gone. Captain Briggs, his wife, their two-year-old daughter and seven crew were never seen again.

shorts.title: Three Lighthouse Keepers Vanished in 1900 🔦 Case #13 Meatball Investigates
shorts.description:
A ship reached a lighthouse, and all three keepers were gone. On 26 December 1900 the relief ship Hesperus reached the Flannan Isles lighthouse in Scotland's Outer Hebrides. All three keepers were gone, the clocks had stopped and one coat still hung inside. The official inquiry concluded they were most likely swept away by a huge wave. The 'uneaten meal' comes from Wilfrid Gibson's 1912 poem 'Flannan Isle'.

#shorts #meatballinvestigates #weirdhistory #mystery #meatballmyths

shorts.title: The CIA Stole a Soviet Submarine 🔍 Case #8
shorts.description:
A ship lowered a giant claw three miles into the Pacific. Project Azorian: in 1974 the CIA used the Hughes Glomar Explorer, sold to the world as Howard Hughes's deep-sea mining ship, to lift part of the sunken Soviet submarine K-129 from about 16,500 feet down. It cost about $800 million. Asked about it, the CIA would 'neither confirm nor deny', and that answer is now called a Glomar response.

shorts.title: The CIA Really Built a Spy Cat 🐈 Case #10
shorts.description:
Spies wired a microphone into a cat's ear, and sent it out on a mission. Project Acoustic Kitty: in the 1960s a CIA veterinary surgeon implanted a microphone in a cat's ear canal, a transmitter at the base of its skull and a wire in its fur. A 1967 memo said cats could be trained to move short distances but not used in a real foreign operation. Ex-officer Victor Marchetti's taxi story was disputed by ex-CIA official Robert Wallace in 2013.

shorts.title: The Ghost Ship Mary Celeste 👻 Case #12
shorts.description:
Sailors climbed aboard a drifting ship, and there was no one on it. The Mary Celeste left New York for Genoa on 7 November 1872 and was found deserted near the Azores on 4 December, seaworthy and well stocked, her lifeboat gone. Nine of 1,701 barrels of alcohol were empty. Arthur Conan Doyle's 1884 story renamed her 'Marie Celeste', and that spelling stuck.

shorts.title: The Cardiff Giant: America's Greatest Hoax 🗿 Case #14
shorts.description:
Two men digging a well hit a stone foot, and then a ten-foot stone man. On 16 October 1869 well-diggers on William Newell's farm in Cardiff, New York, uncovered a 10-foot stone man. Visitors paid 50 cents to see it. It was a gypsum statue carved for tobacconist George Hull and buried a year earlier. Yale paleontologist Othniel Marsh called it 'a most decided humbug'. P.T. Barnum made his own copy, and David Hannum is the one quoted saying 'There's a sucker born every minute'.

#shorts #meatballinvestigates #weirdhistory #mystery #meatballmyths
